title: NIH Terminates ~2,500 Research Grants, Cuts $5 Billion in Funding
synopsis: Between January and June 2025, the Trump administration terminated approximately 2,500 National Institutes of Health research grants totaling nearly $5 billion, per Senate Appropriations Committee Vice Chair Sen. Patty Murray. A JAMA analysis covering just February 28 to April 8 documented 694 cancellations worth $1.81 billion, with the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases losing nearly $506 million alone. A federal judge in Boston ruled on June 16, 2025 that the NIH had violated federal law by arbitrarily canceling over $1 billion in grants due to perceived DEI connections, finding the government was 'bearing down on people of color' and LGBT people. The NIH simultaneously fired or pushed out nearly 5,000 employees, and the administration proposed slashing the agency's budget by $17 billion — a 38% reduction.

title: NSF Cancels 1,000+ Research Grants Worth $739M, Halts All Funding
synopsis: In April and May 2025, the National Science Foundation terminated over 1,000 active research grants worth approximately $739 million, targeting grants related to DEI, misinformation and disinformation research, and environmental justice. More than 400 awards were canceled in a single batch on April 18–22, 2025, based on form letters stating the grants no longer 'effectuate program goals or agency priorities.' On April 30, NSF instructed staff to stop awarding all new funding and disbursing payments on existing grants with no stated timeline for resumption — a move that threatened to affect roughly 40,000 active NSF-funded researchers. NSF's director abruptly resigned on April 24, and a federal court in California issued a preliminary injunction on June 23 requiring reinstatement of grants to 45 institutions.

sources.title: National Science Foundation Terminates Hundreds of Active Research Awards

title: CDC Orders Withdrawal of Scientific Papers, Bans Unauthorized Publication
synopsis: On January 31, 2025, the CDC's chief science officer emailed all division heads ordering withdrawal of all papers submitted to external scientific journals for a political review to comply with Trump's executive order recognizing only two biological sexes. By February 13, the ban had expanded to all CDC research regardless of subject matter, with staff verbally instructed that no papers could be submitted to outside journals 'for the time being.' Political appointees at HHS simultaneously took control of the CDC's flagship Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report, dictating content, withholding three completed studies on the H5N1 bird flu outbreak for weeks, and ordering unrelated wildfire-health studies rushed to publication at Trump's political direction. Journal editors publicly condemned the directives as illegal censorship, and multiple CDC scientists offered to remove their names from already peer-reviewed papers to allow publication.

title: Trump Signs Two DEI Executive Orders on Day One, Purges Federal Programs
synopsis: On January 20, 2025, Trump signed Executive Order 14173 ordering the termination of all federal DEI, DEIA, and 'environmental justice' offices, positions, equity action plans, and grants within 60 days, revoking foundational civil rights and affirmative action orders dating back to Lyndon Johnson. A follow-on order on January 21 revoked Executive Order 11246 — the 1965 order banning discrimination by federal contractors — and directed the Attorney General to identify up to nine civil compliance investigations targeting corporations, nonprofits, and universities with endowments over $1 billion for DEI practices. The Education Department dissolved DEI councils, placed all DEI-focused career staff on paid administrative leave, and archived hundreds of DEI resource materials the same day. The orders affected an estimated 45 federal DEI offices and an unknown number of federal contractor programs across the economy.

title: Federal DEI Workforce Purge: All Diversity Positions Abolished Across Agencies
synopsis: Following Trump's January 20–21, 2025 executive orders, a January 24 OPM memo directed every federal agency to terminate all DEI-related offices and positions within 60 days and to begin issuing layoff notices immediately. The Pentagon abolished all 41 remaining civilian and military DEI positions — on top of 147 already restructured or eliminated under the FY2024 NDAA — for a total of 188 DEI-related jobs cut or restructured across the Department of Defense alone, per a Government Accountability Office report released April 17, 2025. The Defense Advisory Committee on Diversity and Inclusion, a congressionally chartered federal advisory committee, was simultaneously disbanded. Across the entire federal government, thousands of Chief Diversity Officers and DEI program staff were placed on administrative leave and subsequently terminated, and all DEI training contracts with external vendors were canceled.

title: Education Dept Drops Book Ban Investigations, Ends Civil Rights Oversight
synopsis: On January 24, 2025, the Department of Education's Office for Civil Rights dismissed 11 pending civil rights complaints related to book bans in public schools, rescinded all prior guidance treating book removals as potential civil rights violations, and eliminated the Biden-era 'book ban coordinator' position. The department also dismissed 6 additional pending allegations and annulled a settlement agreement with Georgia's Forsyth County School District. On January 29, Trump signed a separate executive order cutting federal funding from schools teaching curricula labeled 'anti-American' or promoting 'gender ideology,' defining those terms broadly enough to encompass standard history and health education. PEN America had documented over 16,000 book ban attempts in public schools since 2021, with the vast majority targeting books by authors of color and LGBTQ+ writers.

title: Trump Defunds NPR and PBS; Congress Rescinds $1.1B for Public Broadcasting
synopsis: On May 1, 2025, Trump signed Executive Order 14290 instructing the Corporation for Public Broadcasting and all federal agencies to immediately cease all direct and indirect funding for NPR and PBS, alleging 'biased' reporting. The CPB, which distributes approximately $535 million annually to public broadcasters, was ordered to revise its community service grant criteria to prohibit any funds flowing to the two networks before June 30, 2025. On July 18, the House passed a rescission bill 216-213 — on strictly party lines — canceling $1.1 billion in already-appropriated CPB funding covering the next two fiscal years. On August 1, 2025, the Corporation for Public Broadcasting announced it would begin steps toward its own closure, marking the end of nearly 58 years of federally supported public broadcasting established under the Public Broadcasting Act of 1967.

title: Smithsonian DEI Purge: 32+ Artifacts Removed From African American Museum
synopsis: On March 27, 2025, Trump signed an executive order directing Vice President JD Vance to oversee elimination of 'improper, divisive, or anti-American' ideology across all Smithsonian Institution museums, specifically citing the National Museum of African American History and Culture (NMAAHC) for promoting 'divisive, race-centered ideology.' By late April and May 2025, NBC News documented at least 32 artifacts removed from NMAAHC galleries, including Nat Turner's Bible, items related to civil rights protests, and a diary tied to abolitionist history. The museum's director Kevin Young resigned in April after taking personal leave in March. Lenders of historically significant artifacts — including a Bible carried by Martin Luther King Jr. during protests, owned by civil rights leader Rev. Amos C. Brown — reported the Smithsonian unexpectedly ended their loan agreements early.

title: EPA, NASA, NOAA Scientific Advisory Committees Purged or Disbanded
synopsis: On January 28, 2025, EPA acting administrator James Payne dismissed all members of the agency's Science Advisory Board (SAB) and Clean Air Scientific Advisory Committee (CASAC) in a late-evening email, calling it a 'reset.' Both committees are legally required under federal law and had members with 2–3 years remaining on their terms. A broader executive order signed in February 2025 directed multiple agencies to identify advisory committees for termination; by March 20, NASA, NOAA, USGS, and other science agencies had moved to eliminate or consolidate more than a dozen science advisory panels. NSF announced closure of 12 advisory committees on April 15. CDC's Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices and FDA's Vaccines Advisory Committee had meetings canceled, severing decades-old independent scientific oversight.

title: RFK Jr. Runs HHS: Vaccines Undermined, Autism Commission, Raw Milk
synopsis: Robert F. Kennedy Jr., a longtime anti-vaccine activist and founder of Children's Health Defense, was confirmed as HHS secretary on February 13, 2025, giving him oversight of the CDC, FDA, and NIH. Within his first month he canceled or postponed meetings of the FDA's independent vaccine advisory committee that selects flu shot strains, ordered CDC research into a debunked vaccines-autism link, endorsed unproven measles treatments (vitamin A, cod liver oil, steroids) over vaccination, and directed FDA to investigate GRAS food additive designations. Kennedy also recruited raw milk advocate Mark McAfee to apply for an FDA policy role and publicly promoted interstate raw milk sales despite CDC warnings that raw milk can carry H5N1 bird flu and pathogens linked to miscarriages and death. HHS announced in April 2025 it would launch a 'massive' autism research effort to determine causes by September 2025, driven by Kennedy's false theory that environmental toxins cause autism.

title: CDC Gutted: 20,000 HHS Jobs Cut, Surveillance Programs Eliminated
synopsis: In March 2025, the Trump administration announced the elimination of 20,000 HHS positions — roughly one-quarter of the department's total workforce — including thousands of CDC employees. An Associated Press investigation published May 4, 2025 found that more than a dozen data-gathering and disease-tracking programs had been effectively eliminated, including the WISQARS accidental-death and injury database, the AtlasPlus HIV/STD surveillance tool, and the 17-person team running the National Survey on Drug Use and Health. In July 2025, the CDC's FoodNet program — which had tracked foodborne illnesses for 30 years — was scaled back from monitoring eight pathogens to just two (salmonella and E. coli). The administration also proposed cutting CDC's core budget by more than half and pulled $11 billion from state and local health departments without warning in March 2025.

title: NIH Research Gutted: 2,100 Grants Canceled, $12.1 Billion Terminated
synopsis: On April 1, 2025 — Jay Bhattacharya's first day as NIH director — the chiefs of four NIH institutes were placed on administrative leave, including the directors of NIAID, NICHD, NIMHD, and NINR, institutes collectively overseeing $9 billion in funding. By June 9, 2025, NIH staff published the Bethesda Declaration, an unprecedented public rebuke stating the agency had terminated 2,100 research grants totaling $9.5 billion and an additional $2.6 billion in contracts since Trump took office January 20. Canceled grants covered vaccine hesitancy research, LGBTQ+ health, gender identity studies, COVID-19 research, and environmental justice. Sixty-plus current NIH employees signed the letter warning the cuts 'harm the health of Americans and people across the globe' and 'waste public resources.' Researchers and universities sued NIH in April 2025 to stop further grant cancellations.

title: SAMHSA Dismantled: $1.7B Block Grants Cut, Half of Staff Eliminated
synopsis: The Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) was targeted for dissolution in 2025, with RFK Jr. announcing it would be absorbed into a new entity called the Administration for a Healthy America. Since January 2025, SAMHSA has lost more than half its approximately 900 employees. The agency terminated $1.7 billion in community mental health block grants to state health departments and cut roughly $350 million in addiction and overdose prevention funding. The Trump budget also proposed cutting an additional $1 billion from SAMHSA. These cuts came as overdose deaths in the U.S. had just fallen 27% in 2024 — an unprecedented decline attributed in part to programs SAMHSA supports, including the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline, which served over 10 million people in its first year.

title: PEPFAR and Global Health Cuts: HIV, Malaria Drugs Halted Worldwide
synopsis: Days after Trump's January 20, 2025 inauguration, USAID sent memos ordering contractors to immediately stop supplying HIV, malaria, and tuberculosis drugs — as well as maternal health and contraception supplies — to dozens of countries. On February 27, 2025, the administration terminated more than 90% of USAID programs after a 90-day 'America First' foreign aid review. UNAIDS documented that the sudden freeze caused immediate disruptions to antiretroviral therapy for millions of HIV patients across Africa, where PEPFAR had supported over 20 million people on treatment. A September 2025 Washington Post investigation found that shipments worth $76 million scheduled for delivery through June 2025 — including the majority of antimalarial medication for over 40 countries — were never delivered, leaving supplies stranded in ports and warehouses. Children died in some countries before drug supplies could be rerouted.

title: Measles Epidemic: 700+ Cases, 3 Deaths, RFK Blames Everything but Vaccines
synopsis: In early 2025, a measles outbreak began in a tight-knit religious community in West Texas and spread across New Mexico, Oklahoma, and Kansas — ultimately becoming one of the worst U.S. outbreaks in 25 years with over 700 confirmed cases by April 2025. Three people died: two children in Texas and an unvaccinated adult in New Mexico, marking the first measles deaths in the U.S. since 2015. HHS Secretary RFK Jr. responded not with a unified call to vaccinate, but by promoting unproven treatments including vitamin A, steroids, and cod liver oil, writing in a Fox News op-ed that 'the decision to vaccinate is a personal one.' Scientists warned the U.S. was at a tipping point for the return of endemic measles — declared eradicated nationally in 2000. Kennedy also revived debunked claims in May 2025 that the measles vaccine contains 'fetal debris,' contradicting decades of evidence that the MMR vaccine is safe.

title: CHIP and Head Start Attacked: Children's Programs Slashed
synopsis: The OBBBA signed July 4, 2025 included provisions placing a 10-year moratorium on the Medicaid/CHIP Eligibility and Enrollment Rule, which had streamlined enrollment for over 37 million children covered by Medicaid and CHIP. Georgetown's Center for Children and Families found that 21 states covering lawfully residing immigrant children through separate CHIP programs face a penalty doubling their state share of costs unless they drop coverage. The Commonwealth Fund estimated 1 in 5 children could be at risk of losing Medicaid coverage under the bill's work requirements. Separately, Trump's April 2025 draft HHS budget proposed eliminating all funding for Head Start — a program providing early education to over 500,000 of the nation's most vulnerable children — arguing Congress should not fund it going forward.

title: Opioid Treatment Programs Gutted as Overdose Deaths Were Falling
synopsis: In April 2025, a leaked Trump HHS draft budget proposed eliminating a $56 million annual SAMHSA grant program that distributed Narcan (naloxone) kits and trained emergency responders across the country — the primary tool credited with reversing hundreds of thousands of overdose deaths each year. This came immediately after CDC data showed overdose deaths had plummeted 27% in 2024, an unprecedented decline. SAMHSA also cut roughly $350 million in addiction and overdose prevention funding and terminated the 17-person team running the National Survey on Drug Use and Health, the only federal survey tracking drug use and addiction trends for over five decades. A Pennsylvania harm-reduction center that had distributed thousands of naloxone doses closed; Reuters reported that a narcotics-testing lab had furloughed chemists who tested the potency of illicit street drugs, eliminating critical intelligence for fighting the fentanyl crisis.

title: Bond Market Panic Forces Trump to Blink: 90-Day Tariff Pause
synopsis: On April 9, 2025 — exactly one week after Liberation Day — Trump abruptly announced a 90-day pause on reciprocal tariffs for most nations, dropping rates back to 10% while simultaneously raising China's tariff to 125%. The reversal came after senior advisers Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick warned Trump that the bond market was in near-panic: 10-year Treasury yields surged to a seven-week high, the opposite of the normal flight-to-safety dynamic, threatening mortgage rates and business lending. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer said Trump's market crash had 'vaporized a whopping $104,000 from the average retirement account.' The S&P 500 surged 9.5% on the pause announcement, erasing some — but not all — of the four-day rout. White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt tried to frame the cave-in as a pre-planned 'negotiating strategy,' contradicting Trump's own statement the day before that his policies 'will never change.'

title: US-China Tariff Spiral: 145% vs. 125% in Escalating Trade War
synopsis: Following the Liberation Day tariff announcement, the US-China trade war escalated in a rapid tit-for-tat spiral. By April 9, 2025, the White House confirmed total US tariffs on Chinese goods had reached 145% — combining 125% reciprocal tariffs with a preexisting 20% fentanyl-related levy. China retaliated on April 11, raising its duties on all US goods from 84% to 125%, effective April 12. China's Finance Ministry called the US policy 'a joke in the history of the world economy' and declared it would not respond to any further US tariff hikes. China filed a new WTO lawsuit against the US and rallied other trading partners against Washington. Analyst Victor Gao of the Center for China and Globalization warned that trade between the two largest economies 'will come to an abrupt halt in a matter of weeks' at those rates. A deal lowering China's tariff to 30% was not reached until mid-May.

sources.title: Trade war escalates as China says it will raise tariffs on US goods to 125% | AP News

title: Canada and Mexico Hit With 25% Tariffs Over Fentanyl Pretext
synopsis: On February 1, 2025, Trump imposed 25% tariffs on all goods from Canada and Mexico — the US's two largest trading partners under USMCA — citing fentanyl trafficking and illegal immigration as national emergencies under IEEPA. Canadian PM Justin Trudeau called the fentanyl rationale 'unjustified,' noting US customs data showed fentanyl seizures at the northern border had dropped to 'near-zero.' Mexico's President Claudia Sheinbaum announced 25% retaliatory tariffs on US goods, while Canada announced C$30 billion in retaliatory levies on US exports including OJ, wine, beer, coffee, appliances, and motorcycles. Canadian and Chinese officials characterized the fentanyl justification as a 'pretext' for broader trade protectionism. Canada subsequently added C$29.8 billion more in retaliatory tariffs targeting US steel, aluminum, and autos.

title: US GDP Contracts 0.3% in Q1 2025 as Tariff Chaos Hits Economy
synopsis: On April 30, 2025, the Commerce Department reported that US GDP contracted at an annualized rate of 0.3% in Q1 2025 — the first economic contraction in three years — reversing robust 2.4% growth in Q4 2024. Imports surged at a 41% annualized pace, the fastest since 1972 outside COVID disruptions, as businesses raced to stockpile before tariffs hit, mechanically subtracting 5 percentage points from headline GDP. Federal government spending fell 5.1%. Consumer spending slowed sharply to 1.8% growth from 4% the prior quarter. The Conference Board's Consumer Confidence Index had fallen for five consecutive months, with tariffs eclipsing inflation as the public's top economic concern; forward-looking components were already below levels historically preceding recessions. JPMorgan had raised its recession probability estimate from 40% to 60% immediately after Liberation Day.

title: Tariffs Collapse US-China Shipping: LA Port Down 21%, Routes Axed
synopsis: The 145% US tariff on Chinese goods caused a sharp collapse in container shipping between China and the US in April-May 2025. At California's Port of Long Beach, May 2025 imports fell 20.9% year-over-year; the Port of Los Angeles dropped 8.5%; Tacoma, Washington plummeted 39.4%; the Port of New York and New Jersey declined 15.3%. Major container lines including MSC and COSCO suspended at least six scheduled weekly routes between China and the US, eliminating combined annual capacity of over 1.3 million 40-foot containers. The Washington Post reported a 25% slowdown in container ships from China arriving at major West Coast ports in the weeks after the April tariffs compared with a year before. Chinese exporters had front-loaded shipments earlier in 2025, leaving importers scrambling to manage stockpiles, while retailers like Walmart and automakers like Ford warned of supply disruptions for toys, furniture, and auto parts.

title: Trump's $2.8T Revenue Claim vs. Economic Reality of Tariff Damage
synopsis: The Congressional Budget Office estimated in June 2025 that Trump's tariff increases implemented between January 6 and May 13, 2025 would reduce federal deficits by $2.8 trillion over 2025-2035 — but simultaneously reduce real US GDP by 0.6% by 2035 and lower the long-run growth rate by 0.06 percentage points annually. Trump repeatedly claimed the tariffs were generating record revenue and called them 'an American economic miracle.' In reality, by early 2026, the actual 2025 trade deficit in goods fell just 0.2% — not the '78% reduction' Trump publicly boasted — and the trade deficit in goods was actually up 2.1% compared to 2024. NBER economists calculated the average US tariff rate rose from 2.4% to 9.6%, the highest level of trade protectionism in 80 years, exceeding even the 1930s Smoot-Hawley tariffs as a share of GDP.

title: China Stops Buying US Soybeans: Farmers Face Five-Year-Low Prices
synopsis: China — which historically purchased at least a quarter of all US-grown soybeans — effectively stopped buying American soybeans in 2025 as a direct consequence of the trade war. In September 2025, China imported zero soybeans from the US, the first time in seven years that shipments fell to zero; for the first time in over 20 years, China did not buy from the autumn US harvest. Brazil captured an 85.2% share of China's soybean imports, with Chinese crushers booking 8 million metric tons of Brazilian beans for September alone. Chicago soybean futures fell to near five-year lows. In March 2025, China had already suspended soybean import licenses for three major US firms — CHS Inc., Louis Dreyfus Grains, and EGT — and imposed $21 billion in levies on US agricultural products including soybeans, wheat, meat, and cotton. US farmers were storing crops in hopes of a price recovery, delaying cash flow, while tractor makers and agricultural equipment businesses also suffered cascading losses.

title: Fed Refuses to Cut Rates as Tariff Stagflation Threatens Dual Mandate
synopsis: The Federal Reserve held its key interest rate unchanged at 4.25-4.5% at its May 7, 2025 meeting — the third consecutive hold — explicitly citing Trump's tariff-driven uncertainty as the reason it could not act despite presidential pressure to cut. Chair Jerome Powell warned that 'if the large increases in tariffs are sustained, they are likely to generate a rise in inflation, a slowdown in economic growth, and an increase in unemployment' — a stagflationary scenario that puts the Fed's dual mandate in direct tension. In congressional testimony on June 24-25, 2025, Powell stated he expected 'tariff inflation to show up more' in summer data and refused to signal a rate cut at any specific future meeting. Trump publicly demanded immediate rate cuts throughout this period, intensifying his conflict with the Fed's independence. Powell noted the 2025 tariffs were 'significantly larger than anticipated' and the situation was 'far from' the smaller 2018 tariffs that served as any historical guide.

sources.title: Fed leaves interest rates unchanged despite Trump demands | AP News

title: EU, India, and Japan Retaliate: $109B in Counter-Tariffs on US Goods
synopsis: Trump's tariff war drew coordinated retaliation from traditional US allies. The European Union approved counter-tariffs covering 93 billion euros ($109 billion) of US goods in July 2025, with two packages set to trigger in August and September if negotiations collapsed; the EU ultimately faced 30% US tariffs before a last-minute 15% deal was reached around August 1. Canada imposed C$30 billion in retaliatory tariffs on US exports starting March 4, followed by C$29.8 billion more targeting US steel, aluminum, and autos, plus 25% tariffs on US-made automobiles in April. India filed retaliatory duty proposals at the WTO in July 2025 over US auto tariffs affecting $2.89 billion of Indian exports, then faced an additional 25% US tariff on August 6 after trade talks deadlocked. Japan's Prime Minister Ishiba called the tariffs a 'national crisis.' In total, US trading partners representing the vast majority of global GDP mounted formal retaliatory measures or filed WTO challenges against Washington's tariff regime.

title: Trans Military Ban Reinstated via Executive Order
synopsis: On January 27, 2025, President Trump signed an executive order titled 'Prioritizing Military Excellence and Readiness,' reinstating a ban on transgender service members under EO authority that revoked Biden's EO 14004 of January 25, 2021. The order declared that anyone diagnosed with gender dysphoria 'cannot satisfy the rigorous standards necessary' for military service and directed Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth to submit an implementation plan within 30 days. The order went further than the first-term ban by potentially stripping benefits from long-serving transgender troops, including those with combat tours. Rights groups filed a lawsuit within 24 hours on behalf of six active-duty service members, arguing it violated constitutional equal protection guarantees. The Pentagon identified approximately 4,240 active-duty, National Guard, and Reserve troops with a gender dysphoria diagnosis as the population affected.

title: 4,240 Trans Troops Identified for Forced Discharge
synopsis: A February 26, 2025 Defense Department memo announced that military personnel diagnosed with gender dysphoria would be discharged, setting a June 6, 2025 deadline for voluntary separation with financial bonuses for active-duty members, and July 7 for National Guard and Reserve. The Pentagon identified 4,240 service members — approximately 0.2 percent of the 2.1 million in uniform — with a gender dysphoria diagnosis as of December 9, 2024, far below the previous estimate of 15,000 transgender troops. By early May 2025, roughly 1,000 had voluntarily come forward to separate, about a quarter of those identified; the Army alone accounted for approximately 500. After June 6, involuntary separations began for those who had not self-identified. Defense records showed the military had spent approximately $15 million over five years on gender-affirming care for these service members, a fraction of the $300 million spent on erectile dysfunction medications in a comparable period.

title: Federal Ban on Trans Youth Healthcare Signed Jan. 28
synopsis: On January 28, 2025, Trump signed 'Protecting Children from Chemical and Surgical Mutilation,' directing all federal agencies to halt funding, sponsorship, or support for gender-affirming care for people under 19. The order directed HHS to rescind its 2022 guidance on gender-affirming care, required DoD to exclude trans youth care from TRICARE coverage, and mandated federal employee health benefit plans (FEHB/PSHB) exclude pediatric trans surgeries or hormones beginning in the 2026 plan year. An estimated 300,100 transgender youth aged 13–17 live in the U.S., with approximately 180,000 in states where the care had been legally permitted before the order. The ACLU, Lambda Legal, and three states (Washington, Minnesota, Oregon) filed separate federal lawsuits by February 7, 2025; U.S. District Judge Lauren King issued a preliminary injunction on March 1, 2025 blocking enforcement in four states, finding the order unconstitutional.

title: Agencies Ordered to Purge All Trans-Inclusive Language
synopsis: Executive Order 14168, 'Defending Women from Gender Ideology Extremism and Restoring Biological Truth to the Federal Government,' signed on January 20, 2025, directed every federal agency to remove all statements, policies, regulations, forms, and communications that 'promote or otherwise inculcate gender ideology.' A follow-up OPM memo dated January 29, 2025 set a 5 p.m. Friday deadline for agencies to strip gender ideology from websites, contracts, emails, and employee resource groups, and to place employees whose positions involved 'inculcating or promoting gender ideology' on paid administrative leave. By January 31 CDC webpages on HIV among transgender people, the Youth Risk Behavior Surveillance System database, and HPV vaccination guidance had been removed. The order rescinded five prior executive orders and presidential memoranda dating to the Obama and Biden eras, including EO 13988 and EO 14075 on LGBTQ+ protections. The Census Bureau's sexual orientation and gender identity data page also went offline.

title: Title IX Rolled Back on Transgender Students Nationwide
synopsis: On January 20, 2025, EO 14168 directed the attorney general to instruct agencies that civil rights laws prohibiting sex discrimination — including Title IX — cannot be interpreted to cover discrimination based on gender identity, reversing Biden administration interpretations grounded in Bostock v. Clayton County. On January 31, 2025, the Department of Education issued a 'Dear Colleague' letter to all K-12 schools and higher education institutions reinstating the 2020 Trump-era Title IX rule and ordering open investigations under Biden's 2024 rule to be 'immediately reoriented.' On February 5, 2025, Trump signed a separate executive order, 'Keeping Men Out of Women's Sports,' threatening to cut federal funding to any school permitting transgender girls to compete in female sports, directed through a revised DOE interpretation of Title IX. The National Collegiate Athletic Association announced it would align its policy with the executive order. Critics noted that the 2020 rule makes it harder for sexual assault survivors to report and narrows Title IX's jurisdiction to on-campus incidents.

title: Passport Gender Marker Changes Halted by Rubio Memo
synopsis: On January 23, 2025, Secretary of State Marco Rubio issued an internal cable directing all State Department staff to immediately suspend processing of passport applications seeking a sex-marker change or an 'X' gender designation, citing EO 14168 signed three days earlier. The Biden administration had introduced the 'X' marker option in 2022; UCLA's Williams Institute estimated approximately 16,700 people per year had been applying for passports with the X identifier. The State Department removed its 'Selecting your gender marker' webpage on January 21, and NBC News confirmed the department was 'no longer issuing U.S. passports with X markers.' Applicants with pending applications were told to wait for new guidance, creating processing backlogs. On November 6, 2025, the U.S. Supreme Court stayed a preliminary injunction issued by a Massachusetts federal court in Orr v. Trump, allowing the administration to enforce the no-X-marker policy nationwide pending further litigation.

title: CDC and HHS Strip LGBTQ+ Health Data from Public Websites
synopsis: Following the January 29, 2025 OPM memo directing agencies to remove 'gender ideology' content by 5 p.m. January 31, the CDC removed its HIV statistics page for transgender people, the entire Youth Risk Behavior Surveillance System database (one of the largest nationally representative youth health surveys), pages on HPV vaccination, health disparities among LGBTQ+ youth, and National Transgender HIV Testing Day materials. The Census Bureau's sexual orientation and gender identity data page also went dark, causing researchers to begin 'frantically downloading' federal data before it disappeared. The CDC's National Healthcare Safety Network (NHSN) implemented technical changes in March 2025 under its v13.0.3 release, removing all 'gender identity' and 'sex at birth' data fields from clinical reporting systems and replacing them with binary male/female-only fields, erasing historical SOGI data that had informed decades of public health research. Public health experts warned the deletions would permanently impair surveillance of HIV, STIs, and mental health disparities in LGBTQ+ populations.

title: Trans Prisoners Transferred to Wrong-Gender Facilities

synopsis: On February 13, 2025, acting SDNY U.S. Attorney Danielle Sassoon — a conservative Republican who clerked for Justice Antonin Scalia — resigned rather than comply with the order to drop the Adams indictment, sending a 6-page letter to AG Bondi declaring she was 'confident that Adams has committed the crimes with which he was charged.' Sassoon's letter explicitly stated that Adams' attorneys had proposed a quid pro quo and that the dismissal was 'driven by improper considerations.' Five other senior DOJ officials resigned the same day, including the two leaders of DOJ's Public Integrity Section in Washington when the case was transferred there. Career prosecutor Ed Sullivan ultimately filed the dismissal motion to spare remaining colleagues from being fired.

title: DOJ Purges Hundreds of FBI Agents Who Worked Jan. 6 or Trump Investigations
synopsis: On January 31, 2025, acting Deputy AG Emil Bove issued memos firing at least eight senior FBI executives and ordering a sweeping review of all FBI employees who had worked on January 6 or Trump-related investigations — potentially affecting thousands of agents. About two dozen prosecutors at the D.C. U.S. Attorney's Office were terminated. The FBI Agents Association issued a rare public warning that hundreds of firings were coming. By June 2025, Kash Patel had pushed out senior FBI agents with decades of institutional knowledge, disbanded the premier public corruption unit, and reoriented the entire bureau toward immigration enforcement, while agents were subjected to expanded polygraph testing to identify leakers.

title: DOJ Fires Over 139 Immigration Judges in Ongoing Purge
synopsis: Beginning February 15, 2025, the Trump administration started firing immigration judges without explanation, dismissing 20 in the first wave including 13 who had not yet been sworn in. Firings continued throughout the year: by October 2025, CNN reported 139 immigration judges had been fired, taken early-out offers, or been involuntarily transferred out of the approximately 700 nationwide. Analysis showed at least 30 dismissed judges had asylum grant rates of 30% or higher, suggesting a pattern of removing judges perceived as too lenient. The firings led to immigration case delays extending to 2029 and a growing backlog of nearly 4 million cases, even as Congress had authorized $3 billion to hire additional judges.

title: DOJ Indicts NY AG Letitia James; Federal Judge Dismisses Case as Unlawfully Filed
synopsis: In August 2025, the DOJ convened a grand jury and subpoenaed New York AG Letitia James' office for documents relating to her civil fraud case against Trump and her case against the NRA. On October 9, 2025 — days after Trump publicly complained on Truth Social that James had not yet been charged — the U.S. Attorney's office for the Eastern District of Virginia indicted James on mortgage fraud charges. James called it 'the most blatant example of this administration carrying out the president's political retribution campaign.' On November 24, 2025, U.S. District Judge Cameron McGowan Currie dismissed the case, ruling that the prosecutor — Trump loyalist Lindsey Halligan — had been unlawfully appointed as interim U.S. Attorney. A grand jury subsequently declined to re-indict James twice, including a second refusal on December 11, 2025.

title: Trump Threatens Military Force to Seize Greenland from Denmark
synopsis: On January 7, 2025, President-elect Trump held a press conference at Mar-a-Lago where he refused to rule out using military or economic force to acquire Greenland, saying 'We need Greenland for national security purposes' and that U.S. control was 'an absolute necessity.' He threatened to 'tariff Denmark at a very high level' if Copenhagen refused to relinquish the autonomous territory. Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen held a 45-minute emergency call with Trump on January 15 and told him that 'Greenland is not for sale' and that only Greenlanders could decide their own future. The crisis triggered extraordinary cross-party meetings in Copenhagen and drew condemnation from Germany, France, and the EU, who warned the principle of inviolable borders applied to all nations.

title: Trump Vows to 'Take Back' Panama Canal in Inauguration Speech
synopsis: In his January 20, 2025 inauguration address, Trump invoked 19th-century 'Manifest Destiny' rhetoric and vowed that the United States would retake the Panama Canal, declaring 'We didn't give it to China. We gave it to Panama, and we're taking it back.' On February 2, Trump reiterated the threat, warning of 'powerful' U.S. action and saying 'we're going to take it back, or something very powerful is going to happen.' Panama's President Raül Mulino told Secretary of State Rubio that Panama's sovereignty over the canal was 'not up for debate.' By March 2025 Trump hailed a BlackRock deal to buy Chinese-linked ports as proof the U.S. was 'reclaiming' the canal, though Panama retained full operational sovereignty.

title: Trump Withdraws U.S. from Paris Climate Agreement — Again
synopsis: Within hours of being sworn in on January 20, 2025, Trump signed an executive order directing immediate withdrawal from the Paris Agreement, his second such action after doing so in 2017. The order instructed the U.S. Ambassador to the UN to 'immediately submit formal written notification' of withdrawal, declaring it 'effective immediately upon notification.' The move left the United States as one of only four countries outside the agreement — alongside Iran, Libya, and Yemen — and cut off all U.S. climate finance commitments. Climate experts warned the withdrawal would embolden other nations to backslide and cede U.S. influence over global emissions policy for years.

sources.title: Trump signs order directing US withdrawal from the Paris climate agreement | AP News

title: Trump Withdraws U.S. from World Health Organization — Again
synopsis: On January 20, 2025, Trump signed an executive order beginning the process of withdrawing the U.S. from the World Health Organization for the second time, stating 'World Health ripped us off, everybody rips off the United States — it's not going to happen anymore.' The withdrawal initiates a 12-month notice period and immediately halted all U.S. financial contributions; the U.S. had been funding roughly 18% of WHO's $6.8 billion biennial budget. Public health experts warned the move would undermine U.S. standing as a global health leader and impair pandemic preparedness worldwide. The action reversed Biden's 2021 re-entry and came amid an ongoing bird flu H5N1 outbreak, prompting alarm from WHO and Germany.

title: Trump's 28-Point Ukraine 'Peace Plan' Demands Territorial Surrender to Russia
synopsis: In November 2025, the Trump administration circulated a 28-point peace framework for Ukraine that demanded Kyiv cede the Donbas — including territory Ukraine still controlled — to Russia, accept de facto U.S. recognition of Crimea as Russian, cut its military by more than half, and abandon NATO membership ambitions. President Zelensky responded in a nationally broadcast speech that Ukraine faced 'one of the most difficult moments in our history,' warning the country would have to choose between its 'dignity' or losing its 'key partner.' Trump set a Thanksgiving deadline for Zelensky to sign, with aides saying 'either this, or nothing.' European and Ukrainian officials called the plan 'capitulation'; Putin said it could serve as a 'basis' for settlement as it contained most of Russia's demands.

title: Trump Demands NATO Allies Pay 5% of GDP for Defense
synopsis: Throughout 2025, Trump pressed NATO allies to raise defense spending from 2% to 5% of GDP — more than double any ally's existing target — framing refusal as justification for trade retaliation. At the June 24–25, 2025 Hague Summit, allies agreed to a communiqué pledging '5% of GDP on core defense requirements by 2035,' though the language allowed holdouts like Spain to opt out. Trump publicly threatened Spain at the summit's closing: 'We're negotiating with Spain on a trade deal and will make them pay twice as much. I'm serious about that.' Prior to the summit Trump had again raised doubts about whether the U.S. would honor Article 5 collective defense, sending shockwaves through European capitals dependent on U.S. deterrence.

title: Trump Administration Pauses, Then Cuts Off U.S. Weapons to Ukraine
synopsis: In late January 2025, within days of inauguration, the Trump administration briefly halted weapons shipments to Ukraine as internal factions debated whether to end all military aid. By February 28, 2025, with 50 consecutive days having passed without any new Pentagon weapons package, the flow of U.S. arms had 'essentially stopped,' according to the New York Times. Following the Oval Office clash with Zelensky that day, a Trump official warned all U.S. aid — including shipments already authorized and paid for by Biden — could be 'canceled imminently.' On March 3, the White House formally confirmed a pause 'until Ukraine demonstrates good-faith commitment to peace,' ordered by Trump through Defense Secretary Hegseth.

title: Trump-Putin Direct Phone Calls Bypass U.S. Allies on Ukraine War
synopsis: On February 12, 2025, Trump held his first post-inauguration call with Putin lasting over an hour, announcing afterward that both Putin and Zelensky 'want peace' and ordering U.S. officials to begin ceasefire talks — without NATO or European consultation. A March 18 call produced a Russian pledge to pause strikes on energy infrastructure, again announced unilaterally by Trump. On May 19, Trump announced after another call that 'Russia and Ukraine will immediately start negotiations,' though the Kremlin contradicted him, saying the process would 'take time.' By October 2025, Trump announced he would meet Putin in Budapest after a two-hour call, stunning European allies who had not been briefed, reigniting fears of capitulation to Moscow.

title: Trump Declares 'Crimea Will Stay with Russia,' Endorses Russian Territorial Gains
synopsis: In an April 25, 2025 Time magazine interview, Trump stated flatly: 'Crimea will stay with Russia. Zelenskyy understands that, and everybody understands that it's been with them for a long time.' When reporters asked if Zelensky was 'ready to give up Crimea,' Trump said 'Oh, I think so,' blaming Barack Obama for the 2014 annexation. The administration's 28-point peace framework circulated in November 2025 formalized this position, calling for U.S. de facto recognition of Crimea, Luhansk, and Donetsk as Russian territory. Ukrainian officials called the position a 'red line' they would never accept, and the U.S. thus became the first Western government to endorse Russia's illegal annexation.

title: Trump Uses Tariff Threats to Coerce Allies Over Greenland, Canada, NATO
synopsis: At his January 7, 2025 Mar-a-Lago press conference, Trump announced he would impose tariffs on Denmark 'at a very high level' unless it surrendered Greenland, threatened 25% tariffs on Canada unless it became the 51st state, and promised 'very serious tariffs on Mexico and Canada' over migration. The deployment of trade leverage against allied democracies to achieve territorial and political goals — rather than legitimate trade complaints — marked an unprecedented weaponization of economic coercion. At the June 2025 NATO summit Trump threatened Spain with double tariffs for refusing to hit the 5% GDP defense spending target. European officials described the tactic as treating the entire Western alliance as a protection racket.

title: Trump Refuses to Commit to Defending Taiwan, Abandons Strategic Clarity
synopsis: On February 26, 2025, during a White House Cabinet meeting, Trump flatly refused to answer whether the U.S. would prevent China from taking Taiwan by force, saying: 'I never comment on that. I don't want to ever put myself in that position.' The statement reversed the Biden administration's explicit 'strategic clarity' commitment to defend Taiwan and returned the U.S. to strategic ambiguity. Trump had already told Bloomberg Businessweek that Taiwan 'should pay the U.S. for defense' and that 'Taiwan doesn't give us anything.' Analysts noted that Trump's framing — demanding Taiwan pay for protection like an insurance client — signaled that the defense commitment was for sale, alarming Taipei and prompting Taiwan to pledge increased investment and defense spending.

title: Trump Withdraws U.S. from UN Human Rights Council — Again
synopsis: On February 4, 2025, Trump signed an executive order withdrawing the U.S. from the UN Human Rights Council (UNHRC), repeating his 2018 action that Biden had reversed in 2021. The order declared the UNHRC 'attacks our allies and propagates anti-Semitism,' terminated the U.S. Representative's office, and cut all U.S. funding to the body. The withdrawal came the same day Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu visited the White House — the first foreign leader Trump hosted in his second term — signaling the move was directly tied to shielding Israel from Council scrutiny during the Gaza conflict. The order also cut funding to UNRWA, the main UN relief agency for Palestinians, despite an independent review finding no evidence to substantiate Israeli accusations that UNRWA staff participated in the October 7 attacks.

title: Trump Sanctions ICC to Shield Israel, Threatening International Justice System
synopsis: On February 6, 2025, Trump signed an executive order imposing IEEPA-based sanctions on ICC officials investigating Israel, authorizing asset freezes and U.S. entry bans on ICC prosecutors, employees, and their 'immediate family members.' The order accused the Court of 'illegitimate and baseless actions targeting America and our close ally Israel' over arrest warrants for Israeli PM Netanyahu and former Defense Minister Gallant for war crimes. On July 18, 2025 a federal judge blocked enforcement, ruling the order was an unconstitutional infringement on free speech. The ICC sanctions effectively sought to criminalize international human rights lawyers, NGOs, and banks providing routine services to the Court, extending Trump's legal war against international accountability institutions.

title: USAID Shutdown Kills Hundreds of Thousands, Ends Lifesaving Programs Worldwide
synopsis: Beginning January 20, 2025, the Trump administration froze all foreign aid for 90 days, then terminated more than 90% of USAID contracts — cutting $60 billion in global assistance and dismantling programs covering HIV/AIDS treatment for 2.3 million people, malaria prevention, maternal health, and famine response across Africa, Afghanistan, Yemen, and beyond. A Center for Global Development study published in December 2025 estimated the cuts could contribute to between 500,000 and 1.6 million additional deaths annually. On the ground, BBC and CNN documented maternal deaths in Afghanistan after 400+ medical clinics closed, spiking malaria mortality in northern Cameroon due to antimalarial supply chain collapse, and in Nigeria a twin infant died of malnutrition after Mercy Corps abruptly ended its therapeutic feeding program when its USAID contract was canceled. The Trump administration publicly insisted 'no one has died because of aid cuts.'

title: Trump's Day-One Immigration Executive Order Blitz
synopsis: On January 20, 2025, President Trump signed a cascade of executive orders declaring a national emergency at the southern border, directing the Pentagon to deploy troops and provide detention space, and shutting down the CBP One app — instantly canceling existing appointment slots for hundreds of thousands of migrants. Additional orders suspended the refugee resettlement program for 120 days, terminated Biden-era humanitarian parole programs for Cubans, Haitians, Nicaraguans, and Venezuelans, reinstated mandatory detention pending removal, and ordered immediate restart of border wall construction. The ten-plus executive actions marked the most sweeping first-day immigration crackdown in modern U.S. history, triggering immediate federal court challenges across multiple circuits.

title: Kilmar Abrego Garcia: Wrongly Deported to CECOT, Supreme Court Orders Return
synopsis: On March 15, 2025, the Trump administration deported Kilmar Armando Abrego Garcia — a Salvadoran man who had legally lived in Maryland for a decade with a work permit and no criminal record — to El Salvador's notorious CECOT mega-prison, in explicit violation of a 2019 immigration court 'withholding order' barring his removal there. The government acknowledged the deportation was an 'administrative error.' District Judge Paula Xinis ordered his return by April 7; the Supreme Court unanimously upheld the order on April 10 (Noem v. Abrego Garcia), requiring the government to 'facilitate' his return. Despite the Supreme Court ruling, the Trump administration for months refused to take meaningful steps to secure his release from CECOT, with officials arguing U.S. courts lacked jurisdiction once he crossed the border — a position Justice Sotomayor called an argument for unchecked power to deport even U.S. citizens.

title: ICE Ends 'Sensitive Locations' Protections: Arrests at Churches, Schools, Hospitals
synopsis: On January 20, 2025, Acting DHS Secretary Benjamine Huffman rescinded the Obama-era 2011 'sensitive locations' policy, which had prohibited ICE and CBP from making immigration arrests at schools, hospitals, churches, and other protected sites. A January 31 ICE memo renamed the rescission 'Common Sense Enforcement Actions,' giving field officers case-by-case discretion with no categorical protections. The move immediately spread fear in immigrant communities, with some families pulling children from school. A federal court in March 2025 issued an injunction requiring ICE to follow the old guidelines at approximately 1,400 listed houses of worship across 36 states in cases lacking a valid warrant — but protections for schools, hospitals, and other sensitive venues remained eliminated nationwide.

sources.title: Trump administration throws out policies limiting arrests of migrants at sensitive locations | AP News

title: Alien Enemies Act Invoked for Venezuelan Gang Members, Flights Defy Court Order
synopsis: On March 15, 2025, President Trump invoked the Alien Enemies Act of 1798 — last used during World War II — against Venezuelan Tren de Aragua gang members, declaring them 'alien enemies' subject to summary deportation without due process or immigration court review. Hours after the proclamation, U.S. District Judge James Boasberg issued an emergency restraining order halting the deportations and ordering planes already in the air to return; the administration defiantly continued the flights, claiming the planes had already left U.S. airspace. Over 261 people were deported to El Salvador's CECOT prison, including 101 who were not charged with any gang activity but deported simply for being undocumented. The brazen defiance of a federal court order triggered a constitutional crisis, with legal scholars warning the administration's position would allow the government to deport anyone, including U.S. citizens, without court review.

title: CECOT: El Salvador's Torture Prison Becomes U.S. Immigration Detention Partner
synopsis: Starting March 16, 2025, the Trump administration began paying El Salvador $20,000 per inmate per year to house U.S. deportees in CECOT, the Terrorism Confinement Center, a maximum-security facility where inmates have their heads shaved, are kept in communal cells of up to 100 men for 23.5 hours per day on metal bunks with no mattresses, with no visitation, education, or recreation permitted. Human rights organizations condemned the arrangement as a potential violation of international law's non-refoulement principle and the Convention Against Torture. By July 2025, El Salvador acknowledged to UN investigators that the Trump administration maintained 'exclusive jurisdiction and legal responsibility' over the CECOT detainees. At least 101 of the 261 initial deportees had no alleged gang ties, having been sent there simply for being in the U.S. without documentation.

title: ICE Detains Over 170 U.S. Citizens During Immigration Raids
synopsis: A ProPublica investigation published October 2025 documented more than 170 incidents during Trump's second administration in which U.S. citizens were detained by immigration agents — overwhelmingly Latino. Cases included combat veteran George Retes, held three days without a phone call after a California raid; Florida-born construction worker Leonardo Garcia Venegas, detained twice in Alabama despite showing a valid REAL ID; and Albuquerque resident Jose Hermosillo, held 10 days in an Arizona detention facility. Most strikingly, Alma Bowman of Macon, Georgia, a 59-year-old U.S. citizen, spent 243 days at Stewart Detention Center before being released without a court order. In over 20 cases, citizens were held incommunicado for more than a day; nearly all detained U.S. citizens were Latino.

title: Military Deployed to Southern Border as Domestic Law Enforcement, Posse Comitatus Sidestepped
synopsis: By mid-2025, Trump had tripled U.S. troop deployments at the southern border to over 8,600 active-duty soldiers including 4th Infantry Division Stryker combat vehicles, helicopters, and surveillance drones — at a cost exceeding $525 million. To sidestep the Posse Comitatus Act of 1878, Trump designated hundreds of thousands of acres of federal land in New Mexico and Texas as 'National Defense Areas,' effectively converting stretches of the border into military installations where soldiers could detain civilians accused of trespassing. By June 11, 2025, U.S. troops began directly detaining migrants; over 1,400 migrants were charged federally with 'unauthorized entry into a military zone.' Legal experts warned this represented the most aggressive expansion of military domestic enforcement authority in the post-Civil War era.

title: Birthright Citizenship Executive Order Blocked by Four Courts
synopsis: On January 20, 2025, Trump signed an executive order directing federal agencies to refuse to recognize U.S. citizenship for children born on U.S. soil if neither parent is a citizen or lawful permanent resident — a direct challenge to the 14th Amendment's citizenship clause, settled law since United States v. Wong Kim Ark (1898). Federal judges blocked the order within days; three separate courts issued nationwide injunctions in early 2025. The 9th Circuit ruled the order unconstitutional on July 23, 2025, and the 1st Circuit upheld a nationwide injunction on October 3, 2025. The Supreme Court's June 27, 2025 ruling limiting 'universal injunctions' complicated enforcement of the blocks without overturning them, leaving the order universally suspended as of August 2026.

title: Remain in Mexico Reinstated, Asylum Effectively Ended at the Border
synopsis: On January 20–21, 2025, the Trump administration reinstated the Migrant Protection Protocols (MPP) via Executive Order 14165 and a DHS directive, requiring non-Mexican asylum seekers to return to Mexico while U.S. cases are adjudicated — replicating a policy that during Trump's first term left tens of thousands of asylum seekers stranded in dangerous Mexican border cities for years, exposed to kidnapping and extortion by cartels. Simultaneously, the administration terminated the CBP One app, ended categorical parole programs for 530,000 Cubans, Haitians, Nicaraguans, and Venezuelans, and suspended the refugee admissions program. Combined with near-zero asylum eligibility, the measures effectively ended almost all legal pathways to asylum in the United States. Courts would block some elements, but the aggregate effect was to reduce legal border crossings to near-zero.

title: Deportation Flights to Libya, Colombia, Guatemala — Third-Country Removals Expand
synopsis: Beginning January 27, 2025, the Trump administration conducted military deportation flights to Guatemala (the first country to accept C-17 cargo planes with shackled migrants), triggering a near-trade-war with Colombia after President Gustavo Petro refused to accept U.S. military aircraft on January 26 — forcing Trump to threaten 25% tariffs before Colombia relented. By May 6–7, 2025, the administration announced plans to deport migrants to Libya — a country racked by civil conflict whose migrant detention centers human rights groups have called 'horrific' — despite migrants having no connection to Libya; a federal judge blocked the flights absent a chance for migrants to contest the move. The program represented an unprecedented expansion of 'third-country removals' to nations with documented human rights violations, raising serious questions under international non-refoulement obligations.

title: Sanctuary City Raids: 'Operation Midway Blitz' and Nationwide ICE Sweeps
synopsis: The Trump administration conducted targeted, high-profile ICE operations in cities with sanctuary policies, deploying Border Patrol agents, the National Guard, and other federal forces alongside ICE. In the Chicago area, 'Operation Midway Blitz' launched in September 2025 resulted in over 1,000 arrests within weeks; AP documented agents storming an apartment complex by helicopter as families slept and deploying chemical agents near a public school. Data from the Deportation Data Project showed that in these high-profile sanctuary-city operations, more than half of those arrested had no criminal record — compared to a third nationally — directly contradicting the administration's stated focus on dangerous criminals. New York City saw 1,900+ arrests in early months, while Los Angeles saw a 69% jump and Miami 161%.

title: Pro-Palestinian Students Targeted: Mahmoud Khalil, Rumeysa Ozturk Detained
synopsis: The Trump administration launched a systematic campaign to arrest, detain, and deport foreign students who participated in pro-Palestinian demonstrations, citing a rarely-used 1952 INA provision allowing expulsion of noncitizens whose presence is 'detrimental to U.S. foreign policy interests.' Mahmoud Khalil, a Palestinian Columbia University graduate and green card holder with no criminal record, was arrested by ICE agents in his university apartment on March 8, 2025 — with an agent revoking his green card over the phone in real time. On March 25, Rumeysa Ozturk, a Turkish doctoral student at Tufts, was detained on a suburban Boston street; DHS alleged without evidence she 'supported Hamas.' An immigration judge ruled on April 11 that Khalil could be deported; out of approximately 5,000 pro-Palestinian protesters investigated, 18 were arrested, but the chilling effect on academic freedom was immediate and severe.

title: Legal Immigration Systematically Dismantled: H-1B $100K Fee, Student Visas Halved
synopsis: While publicly claiming to support legal immigration, the Trump administration in 2025–2026 implemented the most comprehensive suppression of legal immigration in modern U.S. history. In September 2025 Trump imposed a $100,000 fee on H-1B visa sponsorships, effectively pricing out small employers; the State Department in January 2026 suspended issuance of permanent visas for 75 countries accounting for 46% of all immigrant visas; student (F-1) visa issuance fell by almost half in 2025; USCIS paused green card processing for refugees and asylees 'for additional vetting'; and travel bans were imposed on nationals of 39 countries. The Migration Policy Institute projected these restrictions would cause legal immigration to fall by hundreds of thousands annually and could push the U.S. into population decline by 2026.
